quotes.author: Theodor W. Adorno

verification.note: Attribution certain: the closing line of aphorism 18, "Asylum for the homeless". Wording is E. F. N. Jephcott's translation (1974). The German, "Es gibt kein richtiges Leben im falschen", is also rendered "There is no right life in the wrong one", and the two English versions differ enough in emphasis that the German is worth remembering alongside them. Cross-checked against several independent sources; no printed edition consulted from this environment.

quotes.text: Normal science often suppresses fundamental novelties because they are necessarily subversive of its basic commitments.
quotes.author: Thomas S. Kuhn

verification.note: Attribution certain: Kuhn's characterisation of normal science in the opening chapter, p. 5 of the second edition. Written in English. Quoted in this exact form by several independent sources; note that Kuhn's own sentence carries a parenthetical "for example" after "Normal science", which citations customarily drop. Elsewhere in the same passage he describes normal research as "a strenuous and devoted attempt to force nature into the conceptual boxes supplied by professional education", which is the same thought in sharper words. No printed edition consulted from this environment.

quotes.text: Most people think improbable ideas are unimportant, but the only thing that’s important is something that’s improbable.
quotes.author: Vinod Khosla

verification.note: Quoted as Khosla's in Sebastian Mallaby's The Power Law (2022), which splits it with "he loved to add" between the two halves; joined here into the single sentence. Two independent transcriptions of the book agree on the wording. The book's epigraph pairs this with "All progress depends upon the unreasonable man" — that half is George Bernard Shaw's, which Khosla is invoking, and is recorded separately under Shaw rather than under Khosla. Date and occasion of the original remark are unknown, so the year is left empty.
